Firstly, middle-aged men were over-represented in the high- relative to the low-lethality group, and laceration was more common than in the other groups (P < 0.01), while drug over-dose was less common (P < 0.01). A history of deliberate self-harm was less frequent (P < 0.01). The incidence of mood disorder (37%) tended to be more common (P = 0.054), but active psychiatric treatment was less common in this group (P < 0.05).
